title.en: KHR_animation_pointer material and camera runtime adapter

summary: Inspect KHR_animation_pointer targets and route only supported mutable glTF properties through a versioned Three.js loader plugin/capability matrix, with visible failure and ownership rules.
objective: Material or camera parameter animation plays only when the exact pointer, accessor type and registered loader capability are supported; unsupported required use fails visibly and never silently degrades into a static claim.
example_prompts: Load glTF material-factor animation through an explicit Three.js plugin.
Audit KHR_animation_pointer camera targets before playback.
Fail visibly when a required animation-pointer capability is absent.
not_for: Core node translation, rotation, scale and morph-weight channels already handled by base glTF animation.
Treating arbitrary extras pointers as safe executable behavior.

principles: KHR_animation_pointer standardizes transport targets; it does not guarantee that a particular Three.js loader build maps every mutable property to the intended runtime object.

Capability is three-part: the asset declares extension use, the pointer and accessor satisfy the Khronos object model, and the registered loader/plugin version resolves that pointer to a supported runtime binding.

Property ownership still applies. Do not animate a material factor or camera parameter simultaneously from a pointer clip and application controls unless a composition policy explicitly arbitrates the channel.
implementation: In Blender, if the chosen exporter exposes an animation-pointer path, record its exact version and compatible export mode, then inspect the exported animations, extensionsUsed/extensionsRequired, pointer strings, target property presence, sampler interpolation and output accessor types. Do not infer support from a moving Blender viewport or from a different exporter’s documentation.

At application startup, record Three.js revision, GLTFLoader revision and animation-pointer plugin package/commit. Register the plugin before parsing. The current official GLTFLoader page lists KHR_animation_pointer under external user plugins rather than built-in extensions, so absence of registration is a capability failure for this path.

Allowlist reviewed pointer families such as declared material factors or camera fields; resolve them against the loaded asset/runtime mapping and reject undefined, immutable, incompatible or application-specific extras unless a separate resolver contract exists.

If the extension is required and unsupported, stop with an actionable error naming extension, pointer and version. If optional, retain the declared static property and label the missing animation; never claim that core GLTFLoader supplied the motion.
observable_checks: A minimal baseColorFactor pointer and a perspective-camera field-of-view pointer match the inspected glTF accessors and change only their owned runtime properties under the registered compatible plugin.
The same fixtures without plugin registration produce the declared unsupported-capability result; they are not reported as successfully animated because the model loaded.

Within one animation, an invalid pointer, an absent property without a spec-defined default and present enclosing object, mismatched accessor type, duplicate/overlapping target, or unallowlisted extras pointer fails preflight with a specific diagnostic.
Application control of a pointer-owned camera/material channel follows the declared arbitration policy and reset restores the transported default.

creative_affordances: Pointer animation can drive designed material transitions, camera optics or extension properties supported by the chosen stack.
Custom resolvers remain possible as separately reviewed application adapters.
known_limits: The official Three.js documentation describes KHR_animation_pointer through an external user plugin, not built-in GLTFLoader support.
Exporter production of KHR_animation_pointer is tool, version and mode dependent; verify the selected exporter from its own primary documentation or inspected output.
No export, plugin install, load, pointer resolution or playback was run.

claims.statement: KHR_animation_pointer is a ratified glTF extension that targets mutable asset properties through JSON pointers; the target path is pointer, node is omitted, pointer properties must exist or have a defined default while their enclosing object is present, accessor values must match the object-model type, and one animation may not target the same property more than once including array/element overlap.
claims.scope: Ratified Khronos KHR_animation_pointer specification on main as read 2026-09-08; application-specific extras interpretation and runtime mapping are outside the portable core contract.

source_refs.locator: Status, Overview, Operation and Extension Usage

claims.statement: The current official Three.js GLTFLoader documentation lists KHR_animation_pointer as supported by an external user plugin, while the referenced Needle plugin documents registering GLTFAnimationPointerExtension through loader.register and identifies material, camera, light and morph targets among its mappings.
claims.scope: Live Three.js GLTFLoader documentation and Needle plugin main README read 2026-09-08; this is not built-in core-loader support and compatibility must be pinned and verified for the installed revisions.
